title: backlog.py stage-back ID copies a headless worker's .claude/ staging copies into its worktree, checks and commits them
goal: backlog.py stage-back ID copies the staging copies dispatch named into the worker's worktree and refuses a copy whose base differs from the worktree's file; it runs selfdoc.py check and the item's own checks there and commits the copies alone with KB-Work on work/ID; the kb-sprint skill's run step 3 names it; a test stages a planted copy and finds one new commit holding only it; stage-back ID --check runs the docs check over the staged copies and commits nothing; the worker's brief names it, so its report states problems=0 for what it staged

run: import sys;t=open('skills/sprint/SKILL.md',encoding='utf-8').read().split('## run [SP]')[1].split('## review SP')[0];sys.exit(0 if 'stage-back' in t else 1)
import subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/backlog.py','stage-back','--help'],capture_output=True,text=True);sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==0 and '--check' in p.stdout else 1)

gates.question: Which Self-Reviewed trailer does the commit stage-back makes carry: the docs the orchestrator names with --self-reviewed, every doc selfdoc.py stale lists, or none?
options: named by --self-reviewed, refused when stale lists another
gates.recommendation: named by --self-reviewed, refused when stale lists another
gates.answer: named by --self-reviewed, refused when stale lists another

gates.question: How does stage-back --check run the docs check over staged copies without leaving them in the worktree: copy them in and restore the originals afterwards, or check a temporary copy of the worktree?
options: copy in and restore the originals, refused on a dirty worktree
check a temporary copy of the worktree
gates.recommendation: copy in and restore the originals, refused on a dirty worktree
gates.answer: copy in and restore the originals, refused on a dirty worktree

notes: Retrospective of SP-sbdy4hsx: every code story touched .claude/ files, so the orchestrator copied each worker's staging copies back by hand (13 files over 4 items), ran selfdoc.py check and the item's checks there, and wrote a second commit with Self-Reviewed for each. Recurred: SP-etslk6yu close (ST-f2n2h22c's kb-census and kb-refresh SKILL.md copies); SP-htl7jkrm (a hand copy-back without Self-Reviewed stopped ST-65r3cwix's land at step stale; ST-qigkeiv3 and BG-6ecranz3 needed the same). Absorbs ST-v5fdysq2 (2026-10-12 triage): only the orchestrator's copy-back caught a dead heading reference in a staged kb-verify step 5 (SP-qg7ncs6d, SP-pbekfhaz); selfdoc.py check takes no staging option, so the worker's problems=0 comes from stage-back --check (clause 6: the test asserts the brief names it). Premise (planner, 2026-10-13): backlog.py stage-back --help exits 2, invalid choice. Gate: the Self-Reviewed trailer of the copy-back commit. backlog.py USAGE in the facade must list the new command or the parser refuses to start. Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 11 of 15, "Worker runs are counted: work and usage rows reach cost, dispatch is safe in parallel, staged copies come back by tool"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
